title: Beef Rendang
subtitle: slow-cooked dry beef curry in coconut milk and spices
excerpt: Rendang is a slow-cooked dry curry from West Sumatra. Beef is simmered for hours in coconut milk and spices until all the liquid has evaporated and the meat is coated in a dark, caramelised crust. It is considered one of the most complex and flavourful dishes in all of Indonesian cuisine.
sourceNotes: Rendang originates with the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra. It is served at ceremonial feasts and celebrations. Traditionally the long cooking process served as a preservation method -- properly made rendang can keep for weeks at room temperature. CNN's World's 50 Best Foods list ranked rendang first in 2011.

content.text: Rendang is unlike any other curry. There is no sauce at the end -- the liquid cooks away entirely, leaving the beef coated in a dense, dark spice crust. It takes time and attention in the final stages, but the result is extraordinary. Use beef chuck or another well-marbled braising cut so it stays tender through the long cook.

items.prepNote: use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 3 lemongrass stalks, bruised and knotted

content.text: Make the spice paste: blend the garlic, shallots, ginger (or galangal), turmeric, cinnamon, and chilli flakes with a splash of water to a rough paste.
Heat a little oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Fry the spice paste for 3 to 4 minutes until the rawness has gone and the paste is fragrant.
Add the beef and turn to coat in the paste. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the coconut milk. Add the lemongrass, cloves, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, for 60 minutes until the coconut milk has mostly evaporated. The mixture will start to look dry and oily.

Continue cooking on low heat for another 30 to 40 minutes, stirring more frequently. The beef will darken and the remaining fat will fry the spices around the meat. The colour will deepen to dark brown. This is the goal. Season with salt and serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Rendang looks pale and wet -- not dark and dry
items.cause: Not cooked long enough or heat too low
items.fix: Rendang needs patience. After the coconut milk evaporates, the oil that remains fries the spice paste around the meat -- this is what creates the dark crust. Increase the heat slightly and stir frequently in the final 30 minutes.

content.text: Rendang is from the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra. It is prepared for weddings, births, and religious celebrations. The dish is now part of Malaysian and Singaporean cuisine too. The long cooking time and specific technique make it unlike any other curry. The dark, dry result is the intended texture.
